title: 🌐 Eryndor Living Atlas XII — Sixthfold World Population & Economic Capacity
rawNotionMarkup: SUPPLEMENTARY WORKING APPENDIX — NOT A SEPARATE DEMOGRAPHIC AUTHORITY. The authoritative sixfold numerical ledger already resides at Eryndor Living Census XII — Sixfold Population & Carrying-Capacity Audit. This companion retains extra analytical notes and a cross-check table only. All previously simulated numeric resident populations have a sixfold current-world replacement. The old source values are retained for provenance, not as current additive figures. The sixfold multiplier represents worldbuilding rescaling, not a sudden event during Gloin's campaign, and it does NOT alter established birth rates. ## World headline - Previous provisional numerical baseline: 343,800,000 residents across 28 modeled peoples and five continents. - Current revised numerical baseline: 2,062,800,000 modeled residents (6 × 343.8 million). - The new geographic planet has diameter 50,000 km, 60% water / 40% land, five continents with Twin Titans shares: Avarra 32%, Orundel 28%, Tharvorn 12%, Sahrad 12%, Vaelora 11%, separate islands and archipelagos 5% of planetary land. Island inhabitants are included in the five continent/coastal accounting conventions pending finer bookkeeping, not added as a sixth population column. - Current global average density across land is approximately 0.657 modeled residents per km², but local density varies enormously. The total remains a planning simulation, not an in-world omniscient census; rare Drakari (previously fewer than 10,000 as separate anchor), Aelwyn, and Living Mountains were excluded from the numeric simulation and cannot be multiplied by a nonexistent precise baseline. ## World population by people and continent — current sixthfold simulation Numbers are in millions of individuals and preserve the existing source table's intercontinental species proportions. Old seven-domain subtotal 22 million → new 132 million (6×), as a subset of the Khazari population, not extra people. - Khazari within Avarra: 133.2 million, leaving 1.2 million outside the seven Throne domain envelopes within Avarra. - Khazari worldwide: 144 million; thus 10.8 million live on the other four continents under the revised numerical model. - Karak-Varn's metro reference: old 3.8 million → 22.8 million in the new simulation. Its previously recorded Throne number and capital number were identical, which creates a domain-versus-metropolitan scope ambiguity. Do not count 22.8m as both a city and an additional entire domain; reconcile the physical metro boundary and its wider foodland while retaining the overall sixfold numerical scale. Village residents are part of totals, not additions. - All seven Thrones remain politically independent; unknown missing holds and the First Throne are not retconned. Older first-Throne reported heights (such as a possible 40m) are historical, uncertain and are not present-day simulation populations to multiply. ## Demography, long lives and birth-rate continuity A sixfold larger present-day population does not mean sixfold annual fertility or that a sudden population miracle happened. The Fifth Age and its different local eras allow varied settlement histories: expansion, state building, disasters, reconstructions, migration and slow accumulated demographic change. All previously established birth patterns remain unchanged. Eldar, Khazari, Aelwyn, Ents and other potentially long-lived peoples may maintain large multigenerational families yet experience slower booms and less violent demographic whiplash than rapidly growing short-lived local groups; do not impose the same fertility on all peoples. No individual's childbearing role, family choice or craft pursuit is altered by these aggregate figures. ## Economic carrying capacity and risk register - Aldermere, western river plains, Orundel river federations and accessible Valtorian agricultural basins: Strong candidates for dense villages, numerous secondary cities, intensive market farming, canals, grain stores, river freight and multi-century urban expansion. Some regions can support megacities; carrying capacity relies on sustained food, water, fuel, sanitation and peace. - Ironspine/Khazari Thrones and Karak-Varn: Huge layered metro caverns and connected surface hinterlands require substantial food imports, deep fungal agriculture, aquaculture, reservoirs, ventilation, sanitation, geothermal/runic machinery and transport infrastructure. Existing magical and technical traditions make ambitious systems plausible, not self-proven; blockade, drought, collapse or political fragmentation still matter. All seven capitals need their own logistics; do not feed 22.8m by one small valley. - Letharion/Eldar wooded realms: Northern forest expansion and long-standing forest stewardship support distributed canopy settlements, cultivated glades and river ports without universal clearing. Some cities rely on imported grain; forest ecological law and ancient habits constrain growth, so no uniform human-density template. - Eastern Urakai grasslands: Pastoral seasonal networks and irrigated river cities coexist, allowing enormous total populations spread across the plains without requiring every Urakai household to settle in a permanent stone town. - Tharvorn/northern coldlands: Densities concentrate in sheltered fjords, temperate southern strips, fishing ports and heated valleys. Far northern tundra, glaciers and frozen mountains stay extremely sparse. Heavy transport and preserved food imports often determine city viability. - Sahrad/desert and drylands: Citizens cluster around major rivers, deltas, coasts, oases, irrigated basins and trade corridors, with massive arid interiors still thinly inhabited. Sudden short-lived prosperity can induce settlement booms and real water/food crises: crop failures, aquifer overdraw, political conflict, famine or migration are possible simulation outcomes, not preset disasters. - Orundel/Twin Titan: Massive fertile watersheds sustain populous federations and market towns, while jungle, impassable highlands, marshes, storm belts and remote steppe preserve isolated ecologies. River flooding, sanitation and disease remain significant even with magical healing. - Vaelora: Great inland lakes, coastal ports and arable temperate districts sustain major towns; Elderwood conservation, Crownwall elevations and far-frontier climates limit density elsewhere. - Veiled Inland Sea: The connected shore villages have local ferries and roads while remaining largely cut off from the exterior; do not automatically place millions inside the concealed ring without a separate habitat, food and secret-transport analysis. - Small states and young fast-growing settlements: It is legitimate for booms in favorable years to overwhelm granaries, housing, aquifers, policing, trade credit and fields. Responses vary: reforms, trade imports, disease, unrest, migration, collapse, sustained prosperity or harsh suppression. Long-lived peoples may experience less severe fertility-driven boom-bust cycles under their existing birth patterns. ## Audit boundaries Population counts are revised simulations, not dates of historical change, automatic outcomes, or canonized migrations. Previous named populations remain accessible in their original gazetteer snapshots as audit baselines; use Eryndor Living Census XII — Sixfold Population & Carrying-Capacity Audit as the single current numerical authority; this secondary appendix must yield to it if a detail differs. Reclassification of towns, full demographic and foodland planning, further new village placement, and updated city infrastructure remain editorial tasks. No change to ancestry mystery, First Throne secrets, player agency or the exact campaign pause: Autumn Day 22 \~11:25 AM, Year 3847 of the Era of Crowns, Fifth Age, Hadrik's desk, Karak-Varn.
